incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired — service=inference-queue-proxy severity=high. Symptom=queue_depth > 2000, avg_enqueue_latency=12s, autoscaler_scale_requests_pending=42. Link: https://monitoring.redwood/inference/alerts/3170004321
Alice Oncall: acked. I'm on it. Pulling dashboards now.
Brian SRE: I'm seeing a hot cell in us-west1, instance spinups delayed. Autoscaler metrics show scale-controller backlog and kube-api 429s.
Alice Oncall: can we do a manual scale to relieve queue? propose bump replicas for inference-cell-654 from 20 -> 40.
Charlie Prod: customers reporting elevated 500/503 on api.redwood.ai — start mitigation ASAP. Can we route degraded responses / cached hits while we stabilize?
Alice Oncall: running `kubectl scale deploy inference-cell-654 --replicas=40 -n prod` now
incident-bot: deploy-controller: scale request accepted. job_id=job-3170004321-scale. Estimated provisioning time ~210s.
Brian SRE: autoscaler backlog looks like a waitloop — scale-controller is queuing requests because nodepool quota is exhausted. Provider returned InsufficientCapacity for spot pools.
Alice Oncall: manual override won't provision nodes if quota/capacity is the issue. Brian, can you request emergency capacity from cloud console? I'll open a PD escalation for quota.
Brian SRE: opened cloud support ticket CLOUD-9981 for immediate capacity. Also triggering fallback routing: shifting 20% traffic to dedicated capacity tag=dc-fallback.
Charlie Prod: Confirm routing change? Need to protect enterprise tenants — @Alice Oncall please confirm.
Alice Oncall: applied routing rule to shift 20% to dc-fallback. Seeing a small burst of 200s while things re-route, queue depth is slowly decreasing.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: initial responder `Alice Oncall` acknowledged at 3170004330. Next escalation to `Brian SRE` if not resolved in 5m.
Brian SRE: I'll spin up on-demand standard nodes in us-west1 (avoid spot for now). Executing: `gcloud compute instances create --machine-type=n1-standard-8 --count=6 --zone=us-west1-b`
Alice Oncall: logs show autoscaler errors: `scale-controller failed: 429 Too Many Requests` — kube-apiserver is being rate-limited. That explains delayed scale ops.
Charlie Prod: If control-plane is rate limited, batch scale requests. For now keep the OD nodes + routing fallback. Also notify support about customer incidents.
Brian SRE: OD nodes provisioned, nodes joined cluster, pods scheduling. Replicas now 38/40. Queue depth halved in the last 2 minutes.
Alice Oncall: verifying customer impact — SLO error budget spikes but no new customer-facing P1s. Keeping PD incident open while monitoring. Updating status page.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: alert auto-resolved (queue_depth < 500) at 3170004405. Alert state: recovered. Please confirm before closing.
Alice Oncall: Confirmed recovery. Queue stable, enqueue latency back to normal. Follow-ups: postmortem to cover autoscaler throttle, quota fallback gaps, and a runbook to avoid on-call manual steps. Handoff to next oncall @Danielle Oncall for post-incident tasks.
Danielle Oncall: ack handoff. I'll own the postmortem and runbook updates.
